title: The wise woman of Abel (2 Samuel 20:14–22)
hookLine: a woman on the wall saves her town with a few wise words
carry: one wise voice saves a city
last: WOULD I HAD DIED FOR THEE.

lines: WE HAVE NO PART IN DAVID.
cards: The battering has already started. Absalom is dead, but the kingdom hasn't settled. A man named Sheba son of Bichri has blown a trumpet and shouted: we have no part in David.

Joab, back at the head of David's army, has chased him to a walled town called Abel of Beth-maacah. Sheba is inside. The army has thrown up a siege mound against the town, and the soldiers are battering the wall.
Everyone inside is about to pay for one man. Then, from the top of the wall, a woman calls out.

teach.h: HEAR, HEAR! TELL JOAB TO COME NEAR.
teach.b: The text calls her a wise woman, and never gives her name. Her first words: hear, hear! Tell Joab to come near, so I can speak with him.
And Joab comes. She doesn't scream at the army or hide in a cellar. She asks for a conversation with the one person who can stop it.
Are you Joab? I am. Then listen to the words of your handmaid.
I'm listening. And she makes her case.
First, the town's name: in the old days people said, ask counsel at Abel, and so they settled things. Second, who she is: one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel.
Third, what Joab is about to do: you seek to destroy a city and "a mother in Israel". Why would you swallow up the inheritance of the Lord? Joab answers fast.
One man, Sheba, has lifted his hand against the king. Hand him over, and I'll leave. She says: his head will be thrown to you over the wall.
Then she goes to all the people, the text says, in her wisdom. They do it. Joab blows the trumpet, and the army goes home.

It's a grim ending, and the text doesn't soften it. But a whole town was about to fall for one man's rebellion. She found out what the commander actually wanted, named what was at stake, and found the narrow way through.

teach.h: ONE WISE VOICE SAVES A CITY.
teach.b: The text records no other voice from that wall. Hers was enough.

how: Jews read the wise woman of Abel as part of the book of Samuel; some readers set her beside the wise woman of Tekoa in chapter 14, and one midrash identifies her with Serah, the daughter of Asher.

o: the queen mother who counseled King David
the unnamed woman who talked a siege to an end
a prophetess who told Joab to besiege the town

games.q: the wise woman of Abel — tap the pairs.
p: we have no part in David
calls from the wall: hear, hear!

s: the text gives the wise woman's name
it calls her only a wise woman.
she said people used to ask counsel at Abel
the town was known for settling things by talking them through.
Joab wanted to destroy the whole town
he said, far be it from me; he wanted only Sheba.

games.q: you live in Abel. an army is battering your town's wall to get at one rebel hiding inside. what do you do?
o: hide and hope the wall holds.
call from the wall and ask to speak with the commander.
open the gates and let the army in.
games.why: the wise woman calls, hear, hear! tell Joab to come near. she learns he wants only Sheba, and the town is spared.

practice: Think of a place where something is heading toward damage: a group chat turning cruel, a decision no one is questioning.

Ask the wise woman's questions: who can actually stop this, what do they really want, what's at stake that they might not see? Then shape one calm, clear sentence and just have it ready; if you pray, you can ask for wise words.

wordCard.voice: Wise woman. The unnamed woman on Abel's wall who asked for the commander and spoke for her city. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a wise woman, as the text calls her in 2 Samuel 20:16.

carryVoice: Your line: one wise voice saves a city. And a mother in Israel was still standing. Until tomorrow.
